description: Deviations from the literal text of SPEC.md, with justification. A deviation is permitted ONLY when the literal text is unsatisfiable or strictly weaker than what it intends, and only when the intended content is proved in full. Every entry names the SPEC clause, what was changed, why, and the declaration that carries the intended strength. Silent deviation is forbidden. A deviation filed against a KERNEL-REFUTED clause is not a permanent resting place: SPEC.md is the normative contract, so a clause this repository has proved false is a defect in the contract and SHALL be corrected there. Entries whose `adoptedIntoSpec` names an amendment id have been so corrected; their refutation theorems stay cited, because the reason the text changed is part of the record and outlives the text it replaced. An amendment is the SMALLEST change that makes the clause true, never a restatement of a weaker theorem the repository happens to have; where the obligation nevertheless shrank, `strengthEffect` says so in those words.

deviations.refutedSpecText: theorem costed_erase_iff_plain_run : Wasm.CostedRun P module invocation costedTrace observation <-> Wasm.Run module invocation (eraseCosts costedTrace) observation
deviations.specText: theorem costed_erase_iff_plain_run : Wasm.CostedRun P module invocation costedTrace observation <-> (Wasm.Run module invocation (eraseCosts costedTrace) observation /\ Wasm.CostedLabelling module invocation costedTrace)
deviations.issue: The literal biconditional is FALSE, and this is now PROVED rather than argued. `costedTrace` is universally quantified, and the right-hand side mentions it only through `eraseCosts costedTrace`, which is not injective: it discards the installed byte count of `enterGemm`, the requested page count of `memoryGrowSucceed`, and it identifies the whole ordinary-rule family in `Event.step`. A trace carrying forged cost labels whose erasure equals a valid plain trace therefore satisfies the right-hand side without being a costed run the machine can produce. The backward direction cannot hold for an arbitrary labelling.
refutedBy: WasmGemmGnaf.Wasm.not_costed_erase_iff_plain_run -- for EVERY profile, not (forall module invocation costedTrace observation, CostedRun <-> Run (eraseCosts costedTrace))
WasmGemmGnaf.Wasm.Counterexample.minimalModule -- a module that passes `Wasm.validate` (minimalModule_validate), together with a three-step maximal run of it (minimal_finiteExecution)
WasmGemmGnaf.Wasm.Counterexample.forgedTrace -- [enterGemm 1, i32Const, returnGemm 0]; the run installs ZERO raw bytes, so the machine's label is `enterGemm 0`
WasmGemmGnaf.Wasm.Counterexample.minimal_run -- the right-hand side HOLDS of the forged trace
WasmGemmGnaf.Wasm.Counterexample.minimal_not_costedRun -- the left-hand side FAILS, under any profile
WasmGemmGnaf.Wasm.erase_enterGemm_eq -- erasure discards the payload the two sides disagree about
deviations.resolution: RESOLVED BY AMENDING SPEC, not by deviating from it. SPEC 7.5 now states the biconditional with the minimal side condition `Wasm.CostedLabelling module invocation costedTrace` on the right-hand side, states the side-condition-free existential law `costed_run_iff_plain_run` beside it, and defines `CostedLabelling` -- a predicate the clause previously used without defining. The side condition is minimal in the sense that matters: it is a condition on LABELS alone (no observation, no store, no terminal status appears in it), so it cannot smuggle the conclusion into the hypothesis, and it is exactly the payload information `eraseCosts` discards. `Wasm.costed_erase_iff_plain_run` carries the amended proposition verbatim, so the binding in Conformance/RequiredSignatures.lean is now EXACT (`-- spec-signature:`) and the SPEC 15 name is DISCHARGED. This entry stays on file: the refutation is why the text reads as it does.

deviations.refutedSpecText: A plan loop iterates a number of times determined by its extent. (SPEC 11.1 stated no rule for a register-bounded loop's trip count at all; the reading above is the one an implementer would take, and it is the one that breaks Plan.steps_le_stepBound.)
deviations.specText: A loop whose trip count is read from a register SHALL clamp that count at the profile's address-space ceiling (`Plan.loopRegMaxTrips = 2^32 - 1`, the released i32 ceiling, equal to `maxRawExtent`), so that a static step bound remains derivable from the plan text alone.
deviations.issue: An UNCLAMPED register-bounded loop would make the pre-existing theorem Plan.steps_le_stepBound FALSE: that theorem bounds executed steps by a static Nat computed from the plan text, and no fixed number bounds a loop whose trip count is an arbitrary register value (take body = setReg and an arbitrarily large extent register).
deviations.resolution: Plan.loopReg runs Nat.min (m.reg extentReg) loopRegMaxTrips times, with loopRegMaxTrips = 4294967295.
intendedContentProvedBy: WasmGemmGnaf.GNAF.loopReg_trips_from_memory -- trip count IS the memory word, given n <= loopRegMaxTrips
WasmGemmGnaf.GNAF.loopReg_eq_loopNest -- agrees with the literal-extent form
WasmGemmGnaf.GNAF.loopReg_zero -- no clamp hypothesis needed
deviations.strengthEffect: NEUTRAL IN REACH. loopRegMaxTrips is the released i32 ceiling and equals maxRawExtent, so the clamp is unreachable for any configuration the released ABI can present or any value the compiled i32 locals can hold. It preserves an existing theorem instead of weakening it. No SPEC 15 name is affected.
deviations.amendmentText: ADOPTED. SPEC 11.1 now states the clamp, names `Plan.loopRegMaxTrips`, records that it equals `maxRawExtent` and is therefore unreachable for the released ABI, and states that the trip count is still exactly the memory word below the ceiling.

deviations.specText: theorem incremental_eq_full_rebuild (hcoherent : Atlas.Coherent state.body) (hupdate : (Atlas.accumulate budget state delta).result = .complete successor) : Atlas.canonicalize successor.body = Atlas.canonicalize (Atlas.semanticRebuildBodyWith state.body.scope (state.body.declarationBase U delta.declarations))
deviations.issue: The literal statement is FALSE, and this is PROVED, not argued. `state` is universally quantified over `Atlas.UnsealedState`, a type that carries neither a scope restriction nor a coherence obligation. (a) SCOPE: `Atlas.semanticRebuildBody` takes only the declaration base, which names no objective, profile or problem identity, so it always answers `Scope.unscoped`; `Atlas.semanticApplyBody` preserves the scope of the state it updates; `Atlas.canonicalize` copies the three identities verbatim. Any state whose objective identity is not `nullId` therefore falsifies the equation for EVERY budget and delta. (b) COHERENCE: a state may record a semantic half its declaration base does not derive, and the surplus survives canonicalisation.

WasmGemmGnaf.Atlas.Counterexample.incoherent_ne_full_rebuild -- the witness for the line above: an UNSCOPED state that records one stray semantic object its empty declaration base does not derive
WasmGemmGnaf.Atlas.Counterexample.scopedState_accumulate -- the update instance used is `Delta.empty`, whose completion is itself required by SPEC 12.5's `update_empty_fixed_point`
deviations.resolution: RESOLVED BY AMENDING SPEC TO THE STRONGER FORM, not to the weaker theorem this repository already had. The obvious repair -- adding both hypotheses the refutations show to be load-bearing, `Atlas.Coherent state.body` AND `state.body.scope = Atlas.Scope.unscoped` -- is exactly the shape of `Atlas.incremental_eq_full_rebuild` as declared in Atlas/Rebuild.lean, and adopting it would have amended SPEC to match a weaker theorem for a ledger point. It was REJECTED for that reason. SPEC 12.5 instead states the general form, which fixes the scope objection by rebuilding in the state's OWN scope rather than assuming it away: it implies the repaired literal form (instantiate the scope at `unscoped`) and additionally constrains every scoped state, about which the superseded text said nothing true. SPEC 12.5 now also requires `incremental_eq_full_rebuild_exact` (the same equation before canonicalisation, stronger again), `semanticApplyBody_coherent` and `rebuild_coherent`, so `Atlas.Coherent` is DISCHARGED at every state the pipeline produces rather than assumed, and it defines `Atlas.Coherent` and `Atlas.semanticRebuildBodyWith` in the clause's own fenced block. CONSEQUENCE, STATED PLAINLY: the gap has reversed direction. SPEC now asks for MORE than the declaration named `Atlas.incremental_eq_full_rebuild` proves. The proposition SPEC now asks for IS proved here, by `Atlas.incremental_eq_full_rebuild_scoped`, but `xtask signature` credits a binding only when it is closed by `:= @<the SPEC name>`, so until the required name carries the amended proposition the binding stays AMENDED and the SPEC 15 name stays OUTSTANDING. The remaining action is a restatement of `Atlas.incremental_eq_full_rebuild` in Atlas/Rebuild.lean as the scoped form; it was not made in the amending change, which owned SPEC.md, this file and the signature bindings only.

deviations.issue: The statement is FALSE, and this is PROVED, not argued. `state` and `core` are universally quantified over `Atlas.UnsealedState` and `Atlas.SealCore`, and `Atlas.SealCertificate` is the conjunction of the seven deterministic checkers of Atlas/Certificate.lean. Not one of those checkers mentions a byte string, a decoder, a semantics or a cost: `attentionCompleteCheck` asks only that every object the state RECORDS is routed by some indexed signature, and it is satisfied -- with every root empty -- by a state that recorded nothing at all. The conclusion, by contrast, is about an arbitrary `candidateBytes` whose evaluated score is within the core's baseline. Nothing links the two, so a seal that declared nothing faces a real candidate it neither attends nor holds a retained certificate about. The gap is exactly SPEC 10.5's universal coverage obligation, and SPEC 12.2 gives the seal no way to discharge it. This is the attention counterpart of the fact `Atlas/CoverageScope.lean` already records for the cover check (`universalCoverCompleteCheck_scope_blind`), now with a counterexample instead of a blindness lemma.

deviations.resolution: RESOLVED BY AMENDING SPEC, AND THE AMENDMENT SHRINKS AN OBLIGATION. This is the one entry where the correction costs something, so it is stated first and without hedging: SPEC 12.2 previously demanded of the seal a proposition quantified over ALL byte strings, and it now demands it only of candidates the Atlas was given. The residue -- that every profile-valid byte string is declared to the Atlas -- is SPEC 10.5's universal coverage obligation, which is stated there with no coverage hypothesis, is required at SPEC 15 as `Universal.universal_sublevel_coverage`, and is MISSING. Moving the quantifier did not discharge it and did not move it anywhere new; it removed it from a clause that provably could not carry it. SPEC 12.2 also now DEFINES `Atlas.AttentionContains`, `Atlas.AttentionRoutes`, `Atlas.HasSoundExclusionCertificate` and `Atlas.OptimumRelevant`, which it previously used without defining -- that omission is what made a vacuous discharge available to a less careful implementation -- and states the two honesty conditions the refutation is parametric in. Within its reduced scope the amended conclusion is STRONGER than the disjunction it replaces: the left disjunct is proved outright at both the core-level and the strictly stronger `attend`-level reading, so no exclusion certificate is needed and none is offered, and the `Atlas.OptimumRelevant` witness is returned so that no hypothesis is idle. The prose rule that an omitted candidate is legal only against a retained proof is UNCHANGED and still governs SPEC 13's pipeline. `Atlas.attention_no_optimum_relevant_false_negative` is still NOT DECLARED in this repository, under any hypotheses. SPEC 15's name stays outstanding, no declaration wears it, and Conformance/RequiredSignatures.lean carries no binding for it -- a binding must be closed by `:= @<the SPEC name>`, and declaring a theorem of a different shape under that name is exactly what this deviation refuses to do. The AMENDED proposition is proved here, under a different name: `Atlas.attention_no_declared_optimum_relevant_false_negative` carries every hypothesis of the superseded statement plus exactly the two the amendment adds -- `Atlas.Coherent state.body`, the standing well-formedness condition of Atlas/Update.lean (established by every rebuild, preserved by every update, and the same hypothesis DEV-004 found load bearing), and membership of the candidate in `state.body.declarationBase.declarations`, which the refutation proves load bearing -- and returns exactly the amended conjunction. The remaining action is therefore a restatement under the required name in Atlas/AttentionCoverage.lean; it was not made in the amending change, which owned SPEC.md, this file and the signature bindings only.

deviations.strengthEffect: THE OBLIGATION SHRANK. DISCLOSED, AND NOT COUNTED. This is the only amendment in the set that reduces what SPEC demands, and the reduction is real: the superseded clause quantified over every byte string and the amended one does not. It was unavoidable -- `attention_no_optimum_relevant_false_negative_is_false` proves no theorem of the superseded shape exists for ANY reading of the two predicates meeting the two honesty conditions, and `honesty_conditions_satisfiable` proves those conditions are not vacuous -- but unavoidable is not the same as free, and the ledger SHALL reflect the loss rather than absorb it. What moved out of SPEC 12.2 is exactly SPEC 10.5's universal coverage obligation, which is stated there without a coverage hypothesis, required at SPEC 15 as `Universal.universal_sublevel_coverage`, and MISSING. Within the reduced scope nothing was conceded: the added hypothesis is not an assumption that the index already holds the candidate -- it says only that the candidate reached the Atlas as a DECLARATION, and the indexing is then derived (`Atlas.attentionEntryOf`) and the routing PROVED -- and the conclusion is a conjunction strictly stronger than the disjunction it replaces. No SPEC 15 name is declared, no signature binding is added, and `xtask claims required` continues to report `Atlas.attention_no_optimum_relevant_false_negative` MISSING.
deviations.amendmentText: ADOPTED. SPEC 12.2 now states attention completeness relative to what the Atlas was given -- over a state whose body is `Atlas.Coherent` and a candidate in its declaration base -- concludes the strictly stronger conjunction of relevance, `attend`-level routing and core-level containment, leaves the byte-universe half where SPEC 10.5 already states it, defines `Atlas.AttentionContains`, `Atlas.AttentionRoutes`, `Atlas.HasSoundExclusionCertificate` and `Atlas.OptimumRelevant`, states the two honesty conditions, requires the class to be shown inhabited by a real candidate the index returns, and requires `Atlas.OptimumRelevant` to be defined from the objective, the candidate bytes and the decider alone so that relevance is not defined through the mechanism the theorem is about.

deviations.issue: THE DEFECT IS IN THE PINNED SPECIFICATION, NOT IN SPEC.md AND NOT IN THIS TRANSCRIPTION. This is the first deviation filed against the VENDORED Core 3.0 source rather than against SPEC.md's own text. The left-to-right direction of SPEC 7.3's biconditional is FALSE against the declarative side as pinned, and this is PROVED, not argued. `Instrs_ok/seq` of `vendor/wasm-spec/specification/wasm-3.0/2.3-validation.instructions.spectec` types the HEAD instruction with the principal relation `Instr_ok` and requires the TAIL's domain to be EXACTLY the head's codomain. The only rules that can adjust a type are `Instrs_ok/sub`, which preserves domain length because `Resulttype_sub` is a synchronised iteration over both sequences, and `Instrs_ok/frame`, which only makes a domain LONGER; both apply to SEQUENCES, and there is no `Instr_ok/sub` and no `Instr_ok/frame` anywhere in the vendored tree. A head that produces fewer operands than the tail consumes therefore can never be composed. `(I32.CONST c) (BINOP I32 ADD)` is the smallest instance: the pinned rules give it NO instruction type in ANY context, so no function body performing binary arithmetic is `Expr_ok`, no module containing one is `Module_ok`, and `DeclarativelyValid` as pinned is close to vacuous while `Wasm.validate` (which implements the appendix algorithm) accepts such modules. THE PINNED SOURCE CONTRADICTS ITSELF ON THIS POINT: `vendor/wasm-spec/document/core/valid/instructions.rst:1357-1366`, at the SAME commit, says the derivation exists and attributes the weakening of `eps -> I32` to `I32 -> I32 I32` to subsumption; that is not an `Instrtype_sub` supertype (the lengths differ), it is `Instrs_ok/frame` applied to the singleton SEQUENCE, a step `seq` cannot consume because its head premise is `Instr_ok`. Rendered prose cannot distinguish `Instr_ok` from `Instrs_ok` -- both print as `C |- ... : it` -- which is why the gap is invisible in the published document and bites only a mechanisation. UPSTREAM AGREES, AFTER THE PIN: WebAssembly/spec issue #2194 ('instrs_ok/seq's principality requirement is slightly over-restrictive', raoxiaojia, 2026-06-22) reports it in the same terms, and PR #2197 ('[spec] Fix instr sequence typing rules to actually be composable') merged the repair as commit bd4633aced30b720ff62b44cf00c03ece792f008 on 2026-06-23 -- nine months after the pinned commit 9d36019973201a19f9c9ebb0f10828b2fe2374aa (2025-09-26). The vendored file is byte-identical to upstream blob bfd71e57ff457c61f546e0a308b99740fda02158 at the pin, so the transcription is not at fault; and the argument is about LENGTHS alone, so no operand-order or list-orientation convention in this repository could create or remove it.

amendments.was: SPEC 5 specified Lean tooling under Tools/ (Main.lean, EmitArtifact.lean, GenerateManifest.lean, GenerateConformance.lean, CheckClaims.lean, CheckAxioms.lean, CheckSources.lean, Reproduce.lean) and stated: 'The Rust workspace ... SHALL be removed after the Lean conformance replacement passes. No Rust code is part of the final product or proof path.'
amendments.now: SPEC 5.1 'Language boundary' fixes two languages. Lean 4 is the proof and implementation language: every definition, theorem, semantics, cost model, plan, compiler and artifact-producing term lives under WasmGemmGnaf/ and is checked by the Lean kernel. Rust is the infrastructure and tooling language: the release gate, source and firewall scans, claim and axiom audits, manifest and documentation generators, mutation suite and reproduction driver live under xtask/ and are driven by the Justfile.
amendments.rationale: Requested by the repository owner. The boundary preserves the property the original clause protected: the trust base stays the Lean kernel. xtask CHECKS whether the kernel has discharged an obligation; it never DECIDES one. A tool that decided a proof obligation would move the trust base outside the kernel, which SPEC 4 forbids.
constraintsAdded: The boundary is one-directional: nothing under WasmGemmGnaf/ may depend on xtask.
No Rust code is on the proof path.
xtask SHALL build with the Rust standard library alone -- a network-fetched crate would be a network-fetched input to release verification, which SPEC 4 forbids.
Rust source SHALL NOT appear under WasmGemmGnaf/, and Lean source SHALL NOT appear under xtask/.

amendments.was: SPEC 4 recorded the WebAssembly Core pin with no note of any defect, and SPEC 7.3 required `validate_bool_iff` against `Wasm.DeclarativelyValid` without saying which validation relation that names.
amendments.now: SPEC 4 records that the pinned revision carries a known upstream defect in its instruction-sequence typing rule and that the pin SHALL NOT be advanced on account of it. SPEC 7.3 states the defect in full, and requires: `Wasm.DeclarativelyValid` read over the amended `Instr_ok'`/`Instrs_ok'`/`Expr_ok'`/`Func_ok'` judgments; the amendment to be one modified premise and no new rule, propagated through `block`/`loop`/`if`; no-regression theorems at every level; the pinned arity theorems re-proved against the amended relation; no coverage marker on any amended declaration, so the Core 3.0 inventory keeps measuring the pinned tree; and `validate_bool_iff` stated over the amended relation with DEV-006 cited.
amendments.rationale: THE DEFECT IS IN THE VENDORED PINNED SOURCE, NOT IN SPEC.md AND NOT IN THE TRANSCRIPTION. `validate_bool_iff` is the right proposition and is UNCHANGED. What was wrong was SPEC's silence: a reader following SPEC 7.3 as it stood would have validated against a relation this repository has proved cannot type `i32.const c; i32.add`, under which no function body performing binary arithmetic is `Expr_ok` and `Module_ok` is near-vacuous. Upstream agrees, after the pin: WebAssembly/spec issue #2194 and PR #2197, merged as bd4633aced30b720ff62b44cf00c03ece792f008, nine months after the pinned commit 9d36019973201a19f9c9ebb0f10828b2fe2374aa.
amendments.strengthEffect: STRICTLY WIDER DECLARATIVE SIDE, BOUNDED AND DISCLOSED. Widening is unavoidable and is the safe direction here: the pinned relation cannot type ordinary WebAssembly, so a theorem quantified over pinned-valid modules would be the most dangerous kind of vacuity. The widening is bounded by the no-regression theorems in one direction and by the re-proved arity theorems in the other, so composability was bought by supplying operands from the frame and not by letting a domain shrink.
amendments.ledgerEffect: NONE. `Wasm.validate_iff_declarative` stays OUTSTANDING and CIRCULAR, the Core 3.0 inventory is unchanged because no coverage marker is attached to an amended declaration, and the pin in authority/manifest.json is not moved.

amendments.was: SPEC 11.1 listed loop nests among the constructs a plan represents and stated no rule for the trip count of a register-bounded loop.
amendments.now: A loop whose trip count is read from a register SHALL clamp that count at the profile's address-space ceiling (`Plan.loopRegMaxTrips = 2^32 - 1`, the released i32 ceiling, equal to `maxRawExtent`), so that a static step bound remains derivable from the plan text alone; the trip count is still exactly the memory word below the ceiling.
amendments.rationale: An unclamped register-bounded loop would falsify `Plan.steps_le_stepBound`, which bounds executed steps by a Nat computed from the plan text; no fixed number bounds a loop whose trip count is an arbitrary register value.
amendments.strengthEffect: NEUTRAL IN REACH. The ceiling equals `maxRawExtent` and is unreachable for any configuration the released ABI can present or any value the compiled i32 locals can hold. The clamp preserves an existing theorem instead of weakening one.
amendments.ledgerEffect: NONE. No SPEC 15 name is affected.
